title: Accelerated Atomistic Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations of Resistive Memory Arrays
problem: Simulating resistive switching memory devices requires modeling frameworks that can accurately treat the motion of point defects across nanoscale domains under external fields. Current approaches lack scalability to reach realistic array sizes with full atomistic resolution.
motivation: Atomistic simulation of emerging resistive memory devices is critical for validating device designs against fabricated structures.
method: Develops a field-driven Kinetic Monte Carlo (d-KMC) code that simulates discrete structural evolution of atomic coordinates under external potential and heat fields. Implements on the GPU partition of LUMI Supercomputer, exploiting high-speed node-local GPU interconnects for efficient global communication. Applies methodology to the HfOx material stack used in resistive switching memory cells.
key_novelty: First scalable GPU-accelerated d-KMC code that efficiently handles field-driven dynamics with inter-GPU communication for atomistic simulation of resistive memory arrays.
contributions: First scalable GPU-accelerated d-KMC simulation code for resistive memory arrays at atomistic resolution
Demonstration of 3×3 resistive switching memory cell arrays with >1 million atoms matching fabricated device dimensions
Efficient exploitation of high-speed node-local GPU interconnects for global communication in field-driven KMC methods
Application to technologically relevant HfOx material stack

metrics.other: first atomistic simulation of 3×3 resistive memory arrays with >1M atoms at device-matching scale

primary_theme: GPU-accelerated atomistic kinetic monte carlo for emerging memory devices
